summary: This document optimizes the link quality mechanism of the MANET Neighborhood Discovery Protocol (NHDP), which can ignore neighbors with poor measured link quality. The change reduces overhead while still keeping correct information about the neighborhood.

eli5.summary: Moving radios in a field keep track of who is nearby. This trick lets them ignore weak neighbors without losing track of what they need to know.

questions: how does nhdp handle low link quality
subtitle: An optional tweak that lets NHDP routers keep, but not use, 2-hop neighbor data while a link's quality is briefly too low.

tldr.problem: NHDP can ignore a 1-hop neighbor whose link quality is too low, but it throws away the related symmetric 2-hop information at once. A momentary dip then wipes that data until the next HELLO message arrives.
tldr.mechanism: Each 2-Hop Tuple gets a new boolean flag, N2_lost. When a link goes LOST because of link quality, its 2-hop tuples are kept and flagged instead of removed, and flagged tuples are ignored by users of NHDP.
tldr.outcome: The symmetric 2-hop neighborhood becomes more robust to short link quality changes. The change is optional, and routers with and without it interoperate.

facts.label: Required?
facts.value: Optional, but all changes MUST be made together

today: RFC 7466 is a Proposed Standard from March 2015. It updates RFC 6130 and RFC 7181, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Problem With Ignored Links
sections.content:
The MANET Neighborhood Discovery Protocol (NHDP, RFC 6130) has a link quality mechanism. A router may refuse to consider a 1-hop neighbor as HEARD or SYMMETRIC while the quality of the link from that neighbor is below an acceptable threshold. The link information learned from HELLO messages is kept meanwhile, so the link can be used immediately when quality recovers. A hysteresis mechanism means two thresholds are used.

NHDP also records symmetric 2-hop neighbors. But when a 1-hop neighbor stops being symmetric, the matching 2-Hop Tuples are removed, with no retention for a possibly temporary loss due to link quality. After a short dip, the 1-hop data is back at once but the 2-hop data is gone until the next HELLO message.
sections.eli5: When a friend steps out of range, you keep the page about them but also throw away your notes about their friends. This fix keeps those notes too.

sections.title: Applicability and Interoperability
sections.content:
The optimization is strictly optional and only permissive. It retains information that would otherwise be removed, and does not use it except where RFC 6130 could have used it. In some cases this makes the symmetric 2-hop neighborhood more robust against temporary link quality changes and so yields a more stable network. The only other consequence is that state for some otherwise expired 2-Hop Tuples may be kept longer.

A router that implements it interoperates with routers that implement RFC 6130 without it. The change does not alter what a symmetric 2-hop neighbor is. It only adds state to each 2-Hop Tuple.

Although optional, it is all or nothing: if any of the changes in Section 4 are made, then all of them MUST be made.
sections.eli5: Using the trick is your choice, and friends who do not use it can still play with you. If you use it, you use all of it.

sections.title: The N2_lost Flag
sections.content:
The 2-Hop Set gains one element in each 2-Hop Tuple: N2_lost, a boolean that mirrors the state of the corresponding Link Tuple.

  • If L_status = SYMMETRIC (so L_lost = false), then N2_lost = false.
  • If L_SYM_time has not expired and L_lost = true (so L_status = LOST), then N2_lost = true.

In all other cases there are no such 2-Hop Tuples. The new state and the retained tuples are reflected in the tables of the updated NHDP-MIB module.
sections.eli5: Each note about a friend's friend gets a small sticker. Green means use it, red means keep it but do not use it for now.

sections.title: Changes to RFC 6130 Processing
sections.content:
In HELLO message processing (Section 12.6 of RFC 6130), the test L_status = SYMMETRIC becomes L_SYM_time not expired, and a new 2-Hop Tuple is created with N2_lost := L_lost.

In the Information Base changes (Section 13), the trigger becomes a Link Tuple's L_status changing from SYMMETRIC, L_SYM_time expiring, or the Link Tuple being removed. The Section 13.2 actions MUST be performed before the Section 13.3 actions for that Link Tuple. Section 13.2 now says, for each Link Tuple with L_SYM_time not expired:

  • If L_SYM_time expires or the tuple is removed, remove each 2-Hop Tuple on the same MANET interface whose N2_neighbor_iface_addr_list contains one or more addresses in L_neighbor_iface_addr_list.
  • If L_status changes from SYMMETRIC to LOST because L_lost is set to true, set N2_lost := true on those same 2-Hop Tuples instead.

The constraints in Appendix B of RFC 6130 change too: each 2-Hop Tuple MUST have a Link Tuple on the same interface with matching address list, L_SYM_time not expired and L_lost = N2_lost.
sections.eli5: When a link just gets weak, the notes are marked red and kept. Only when the friend is really gone for good are the notes thrown away.

sections.title: Impact on OLSRv2
sections.content:
If an RFC 6130 implementation hides every 2-Hop Tuple with N2_lost = true from the protocols using it, no changes are needed to them, including RFC 7181 (OLSRv2). If instead all tuples are visible, those protocols MUST ignore the ones with N2_lost = true.

OLSRv2 uses 2-hop information for Multipoint Relay (MPR) Set and Routing Set calculation but does not send it in control traffic. So an implementation must behave as if a 2-Hop Tuple exists only when N2_lost = false, and as if a change of N2_lost is a tuple appearing or being removed.

The RFC spells this out as edits to Sections 17.6, 17.7, 18.4, 18.5 and 19.1 and Appendix C.7 of RFC 7181. The edits add the condition N2_lost = false to the existing tests on N2_out_metric and N2_in_metric, and treat a change of N2_lost as a trigger. The RFC states this is spelled out because some OLSRv2 implementations are not independent of the NHDP implementation they use.
sections.eli5: A game that uses your friend list must pretend the red-sticker notes are not there. Then nothing in that game changes.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The update only retains and reuses information that NHDP already collected, and only for as long as it could have been used anyway. The RFC concludes it introduces no new security considerations for an implementation of RFC 6130 or for protocols that use it, such as RFC 7181.
sections.eli5: Nothing new is learned, only remembered a bit longer, so nothing new is put at risk.

items.title: N2_lost = false
items.text: Link is SYMMETRIC. The 2-hop tuple is in normal use.

items.title: N2_lost = true
items.text: Link is LOST by link quality but L_SYM_time has not expired. The tuple is kept and ignored.

items.title: Tuple removed
items.text: L_SYM_time expires or the Link Tuple is removed.
